claims.text: One student expectation has students research career pathways using artificial intelligence tools.
claims.quote: research career pathways using labor-market data, online resources, and artificial intelligence tools to evaluate income growth, employment trends, global competition, comparative advantage, technological change, creative destruction, required skills, and possible employers (E, S);
claims.verbatim_quote: research career pathways using labor-market data, online resources, and artificial intelligence tools to evaluate income growth, employment trends, global competition, comparative advantage, technological change, creative destruction, required skills, and possible employers (E, S);
claims.source_title: Attachment, Text of Proposed New 19 TAC Chapter 113 Subchapter C Section 113.26

claims.text: A second student expectation has students explain how algorithm driven recommendations influence spending behavior.
claims.quote: explain how consumerism and marketing strategies, including social media influencers, algorithm-driven recommendations, financial technology platforms, and traditional advertising, influence spending behavior and financial decision-making (Geo/C, E, S);
claims.verbatim_quote: explain how consumerism and marketing strategies, including social media influencers, algorithm-driven recommendations, financial technology platforms, and traditional advertising, influence spending behavior and financial decision-making (Geo/C, E, S);
claims.source_title: Attachment, Text of Proposed New 19 TAC Chapter 113 Subchapter C Section 113.26

claims.text: A third student expectation has students appraise automated investment platforms by analyzing their algorithmic limitations.
claims.quote: appraise responsible use of financial technology through automated investment platforms, including robot-advisors and micro-investing apps, by analyzing fee structures, investment strategies, algorithmic limitations, and suitability for different investor profiles (E, S);
claims.verbatim_quote: appraise responsible use of financial technology through automated investment platforms, including robot-advisors and micro-investing apps, by analyzing fee structures, investment strategies, algorithmic limitations, and suitability for different investor profiles (E, S);
claims.source_title: Attachment, Text of Proposed New 19 TAC Chapter 113 Subchapter C Section 113.26

The page never ties either date to either body in words. c5 carries the date line the page prints and nothing asserts which body sat on it. The weekday is date arithmetic and belongs in compute.py, never in a sentence a model wrote.

rejected.finding: The attachment is the adopted course text.
rejected.reason: It heads itself Text of Proposed New 19 TAC, its url sits in the June meeting folder, and the item itself says changes are recommended since first reading. It IS the one attachment the second reading and final adoption item publishes, which is what c4 and c11 together establish, and that is all any frame may say.

absence_method.document: Texas State Board of Education news release, Completes K-12 Social Studies TEKS Revision, Adopts New Personal Financial Literacy Standards
absence_method.how: The served HTML was saved to disk and read as bytes this run, script and style stripped, tags removed, entities unescaped. Case insensitive counts over the WHOLE page including navigation, headings, link text and footer returned zero for artificial, algorithm, machine learning and automated, zero matches for the standalone token AI, and zero for the stem technolog. The fact-checker reached the same result independently through a separate fetch.

story: At second reading and final adoption the board took a course that has students research career pathways using artificial intelligence tools, and explain how algorithm driven recommendations influence spending behavior, and appraise automated investment platforms by analyzing their algorithmic limitations, in a personal financial literacy course whose own news release names no technology at all.
